expectations.text: Every finding carries a severity grade
expectations.evidence: Report defines a four-level severity scale (Critical/High/Medium/Low) and files every finding under a severity heading: C1-C3 under Critical, H1-H4 under High, M1-M4 under Medium, L1-L2 under Low. No ungraded findings.

expectations.text: Every finding includes a concrete failure scenario tied to downstream harm, not a vague concern
expectations.evidence: C1-H4 each carry an explicit 'What breaks:' block (e.g. C1: 'a Sev1 at 04:00 CET pages nobody... First unhandled overnight Sev1 turns into a multi-hour outage'). Medium/Low findings embed the scenario inline: M3 'An incident that straddles the boundary loses all context mid-stream', M4 'A US holiday Monday plus the standing nightly gap could leave 18+ unclear hours', L2 'the windows drift an hour twice a year'. None are vague concerns without a stated consequence.

expectations.text: Report identifies the timezone coverage gap: Krakow 08:00-20:00 CET = 02:00-14:00 ET, so 20:00-02:00 ET is covered by neither window, defeating the zero-overnight-pages goal
expectations.evidence: Finding C1 states '08:00–20:00 CET is roughly 02:00–14:00 ET... the uncovered gap runs... about 02:00–08:00 CET / 20:00–02:00 ET, six hours every single night' and ties it to the goal ('a Sev1 at 04:00 CET pages nobody, or pages a sleeping engineer'). The ET/CET conversion and the 20:00-02:00 ET gap match the artifact's windows. Minor wording slip ('gap runs 20:00 CET to 08:00 ET' misstates the start; 20:00 CET is inside US coverage) but the correct bounds are given in the same sentence.

expectations.text: Report identifies Krakow readiness risk: 6-week-old team, no production experience, access provisioning still incomplete before go-live
expectations.evidence: C2 covers access: 'Access provisioning (prod SSH, dashboards, PagerDuty) is "in progress" with go-live "next month"... without it they cannot even receive pages'. H1 covers experience: 'The Krakow team joined six weeks ago and has zero production experience with this system. One week of shadowing... is the entire training plan.' Both match the artifact's Notes section.

expectations.text: Report identifies that the US-only incident-commander pool still wakes US engineers for Sev1s, undermining the success metric
expectations.evidence: C3: 'A Sev1 during Krakow's solo window (08:00–14:00 CET, before US comes online) requires waking a US IC at ~02:00–08:00 ET. That is exactly the overnight paging the plan claims to eliminate... which by the plan's own success metric counts as failure.'

expectations.text: Report contains a retest list or equivalent re-check mechanism for the findings
expectations.evidence: The 'Bottom line' section lists five 'Minimum changes before go-live' — remediations, not a retest list. Two items embed verification (test page acked, runbook executed cold, 2-week checkpoint with rollback trigger), but there is no mechanism to re-check the findings themselves after fixes, and most findings (C3, H1-H4, M1, M3, M4) have no re-verification step at all.

claims.claim: Overlap runs 08:00-14:00 ET; the nightly uncovered gap is six hours (20:00-02:00 ET / 02:00-08:00 CET)
claims.evidence: Krakow 08:00-20:00 CET = 02:00-14:00 ET; US 08:00-20:00 ET. Overlap 08:00-14:00 ET, gap 20:00-02:00 ET = 6 hours. Matches the artifact's stated windows.

claims.claim: US and EU DST changes fall on different weeks, so the gap size shifts twice a year
claims.evidence: US changes second Sunday of March / first Sunday of November; EU changes last Sunday of March / last Sunday of October.

claims.claim: Escalation path pages the other region's off-shift primary as the first escalation step, with no in-region secondary
claims.evidence: Artifact item 4: 'if the primary does not ack in 15 minutes, page the other region's primary' — no secondary is defined in the plan.

claims.claim: Polish public holidays include May 1-3 and Aug 15
claims.evidence: May 1 and May 3 are Polish public holidays and Aug 15 is; May 2 is not a statutory holiday (commonly a bridge day). Minor overstatement, does not affect the finding.

claims.claim: Industry floor for a sustainable on-call rotation is 4-6 engineers
claims.evidence: Consistent with common SRE guidance (e.g. Google SRE book recommends at least 8 per site for 24/7, 4+ minimum per rotation); 3 is below any published floor.

suggestions.expectation: Report contains a retest list or equivalent re-check mechanism for the findings
suggestions.reason: The 'or equivalent re-check mechanism' clause is fuzzy: this report's go-live gate checklist (test page acked, runbook executed cold) arguably re-verifies two Critical findings, making the pass/fail line judgment-dependent. Specify what counts, e.g. 'a per-finding list of checks to run after remediation'.

No expectation checks the factual accuracy of the timezone math or DST reasoning. A report could name the gap but state wrong bounds and still pass expectation 3 on keyword match; require the specific correct bounds (already partly done) plus internal consistency.

eval_feedback.overall: Expectations discriminate well overall; five of six require substantive analysis that a shallow review would miss. The retest-list expectation is the only one with an ambiguous bar.
